title: Inspect schedulers, clocks and execution identities
goal: Separate schedule, clock, loaded limits and job identity.
challenge: Inspect cron/system and user timers without changing clocks or unrelated jobs. Prove a disposable execution identity and explain why LastTrigger alone is insufficient.

steps.command: ! getent passwd ll-s1 && ! getent group ll-s1 && test ! -e /home/ll-s1 && sudo useradd -m -U -s /bin/bash ll-s1
steps.explanation: Create a locked disposable account after collision guards.

steps.command: date -Is; timedatectl status; systemctl --no-pager is-active cron; systemctl --no-pager list-timers --all; systemctl --no-pager --user list-timers --all
steps.explanation: Inspect scopes and clock without changing either.
steps.expected: Cron active; user manager available; lists can be empty.

steps.command: command -v crontab systemctl systemd-run timeout; command -v at || true; sudo runuser -u ll-s1 -- id
systemctl --no-pager show cron.service -p LoadState -p User -p Result; sudo crontab -u ll-s1 -l
steps.explanation: Inspect loaded metadata, not a collected transient service. Empty User means root for system services.

hints: Scheduler identity can differ from job identity.
Require loaded state before claiming configured limits.
review: Retain date/timezone, tools, loaded state and actual ll-s1 id.
Distinguish trigger, process exit and valid report.
coverage: LPIC-1 v5.0 107.2 partial cron/systemd timers; 105.2/108.2 reinforcement; self-reviewed, unscored. No at or full objective coverage.
